title: Finite-time blowup claims for Navier–Stokes and Euler (September 2026)
brief_md:
**What this project is.** On 2026-09-08 OpenAI published a 166-page manuscript, *Finite Time Blowup for Navier–Stokes*, and a Lean 4 repository, claiming to settle alternatives (C) and (D) of the Clay Millennium problem statement for Navier–Stokes: for every viscosity ν > 0 there is a smooth force, compactly supported in space and time, such that the flow starting from rest develops unbounded velocity at time 1 while its kinetic energy stays bounded (Theorem 1.1; periodic version Corollary 10.6). The same repository formalizes an unforced Euler blowup from smooth, compactly supported initial data. The repository's own manifest marks its review status as *self-assessed*. This project is where independent checks are recorded, one exact artifact at a time. It does not award anything: the Clay Institute's process is separate, and OpenAI has said it does not intend to claim the prize.

**What is known (transcribed by the maintainers on 2026-09-08, nothing checked yet).**

- Manuscript: [navier-stokes.pdf](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/32d9f210-8b73-45e0-91bc-82a30aef8a9a/navier-stokes.pdf), 166 pages, SHA-256 `0e779481c4da40bd28d1e642e1d8ca57447d129610df28dfa5a11e9af8ae228f`. Sections: 1 Introduction; 2 Physical description of the blowup; 3 Proof outline (pp. 6–24); 4 Constructing the leading order flow; 5 Correcting the base flow to every order; 6 Auxiliary torus and separation of oscillatory supports; 7 Oscillatory realization and correction of the residual stress; 8 Compactly supported mean corrections; 9 Residual improvement and the local field; 10 Compact forcing and whole-space breakdown; appendices A–C.
- Lean: [openai/NavierStokesAndEuler](https://github.com/openai/NavierStokesAndEuler), head commit `8937a8f4cbc7` (2026-09-08). Lean 4.34.0-rc2 with Mathlib. `formalization.yaml` declares four theorems as proved with `sorry_count: 0` and axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`, review status `self-assessed`. Reference theorem names: `navier_stokes_breakdown_R3` and `navier_stokes_breakdown_periodic` in `NavierStokes.ComparatorSolution`; the Euler result in `Euler.Solution`. The Comparator challenges adapt the Formal Conjectures formalization of the problem statement. Build: `lake exe cache get && lake build`. Comparator: `lake exe comparator ComparatorChallenges/NavierStokes.json` (needs `landrun`, `lean4export`, `nanoda_bin` on PATH).
- Announcement: [On the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem](https://openai.com/index/navier-stokes-solution/). OpenAI reports about 10,000 concurrent agents over 88 hours for the Navier–Stokes result and 17 further hours for the Lean formalization, and recognizes the priority of Alpöge and Buckmaster's forced-Euler blowup, which is a separate result.
- Problem statement: [Fefferman's official formulation](https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/navierstokes.pdf), conditions (1)–(7), alternatives (A)–(D).

**Disputed.** Nothing about the mathematics is on record as disputed yet. The receipts requested below are what put a dispute, or its absence, on record. Questions of provenance, priority and conduct raised publicly around the announcement are not a matter for receipts; they belong in this project's discussion thread, with sources.

**Failed.** Nothing tried yet.

**Next.** The opening tasks: build the Lean project and report exactly what it accepts; check that the Lean definitions say what Fefferman's statement says; read the proof section by section and record what you followed and what you did not; explain the mechanism for non-specialists; do the same for the Euler claim.

**House rules for this project.** A receipt says what you checked and what you did not. "The Lean build passed" is a receipt about one commit, not about the manuscript. "The definitions match" is a receipt about definitions, not about the proof. A receipt on the manuscript names the section and the estimates you followed. Say which models and tools you used, including OpenAI's; that is disclosure, not disqualification. The unforced problem, alternatives (A) and (B), remains open and is out of scope here unless someone posts a claim about it.
